_comment: WS-7A SOFT-ZONE HANDOVER demo: = sitl3_dyn3_vision.json (convoy_3lane world, 3 drones, track_convoy in DYNAMIC mode = track_marker_ids null, shared ConvoyRegistry single-winner CAS) PLUS per-drone advisory SECTORS (sector_deg) and an arena. The new behaviour this config exercises: when a tracked car drives OUT of its owner's sector wedge, track_convoy KEEPS tracking but FLAGS the registry (exited_zone); the orchestrator's per-tick matcher offers the flagged convoy to whichever IDLE neighbour's wedge the car ENTERED (from the exit bearing); that neighbour's acquire loop claims it (registry honours the offer) and the original owner releases on its next renew. If no neighbour is idle, the convoy stays flagged and its owner keeps tracking (the 'keep tracking but flagged' path). SECTORS are [center_deg, half_width_deg] (deg, CCW+, 0=+north, bearing-from-C2 convention) and are ADVISORY ONLY (SectorGuard never hard-cuts; the soft-zone flag is the only behaviour). They need an arena (C2 origin) -> arena_name sitl_handover (a 3-wedge fan around C2; mirror of the convoy_3lane / sitl_landing frame: arena north = gz +Y, east = gz +X, C2 at gz origin). The DEMO is driven by a curving CONVOY_ROUTE (sim/run_vision.sh handover3): the cars drive a slow arc that carries a car across a wedge boundary mid-run, so the matcher hands it over to the idle neighbour. WEDGES + ROUTE are GATE-F TUNABLE (the gz lane bearings depend on the spawn poses + car speed; measure on the VM and reshape, NEVER touch code). Separation is satisfied two ways here (distinct altitude_band_m AND sector_deg on every drone) — the bands keep the gz vertical-separation the world needs; the sectors drive the handover. Endpoints/ports/timeouts identical to sitl3_dyn3_vision.json. Pure handover logic is unit-proven (test_convoy_registry / test_track_convoy / test_orchestrator WS-7A); this config is the gz INTEGRATION rig.

drones._sector_comment: alpha owns the NORTH lane wedge (car_7 @ gz 4.2,0 -> bearing-from-C2 ~0). Wide enough to hold its own lane, narrow enough that the curving car crosses OUT of it into bravo's east wedge mid-run. GATE-F: measure the real gz lane bearing and reshape.
bravo owns the EAST lane wedge (car_23 @ gz -2,3.5). A car arcing east out of alpha's north wedge enters here; if bravo is idle it accepts the handover.
charlie owns the WEST lane wedge (car_88 @ gz -2,-3.5).
